body:
Running the installer or updater from a linked git worktree now leaves your global board launcher untouched instead of pointing it at a temporary worktree. Previously, the installer only skipped system temp folders, so any background worker updating the kit from its worktree silently overwrote the launcher and broke it once that worktree was cleaned up.

### Why `~/.local/bin/board` changed to a worktree
When a part runs `install.py . --update` inside a linked git worktree (`~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/worktrees/...`, `.claude/worktrees/...`, or a sibling worktree like `/home/anon/board-a1`), `install_cmd()` previously only checked `under_tempdir(t)`. Because linked worktrees live outside `/tmp`, it rewrote `~/.local/bin/board` to `exec "<worktree>/.kit/up" "$@"`, breaking the launcher once the worktree was deleted.

### What changed
- `install.py`:
  - Added `is_git_worktree(t)` checking agent worktree paths (`/.gemini/antigravity-cli/worktrees/`, `/.claude/worktrees/`), `.git` as a file, and `git -C <t> rev-parse --git-dir --git-common-dir` differing after realpath resolution.
  - Updated `install_cmd()` to skip writing `~/.local/bin/<cmd>` when `KIT_BIN_DIR` is unset and `is_git_worktree(t)` is true, logging `SKIPPED command \`<cmd>\`: <t> is a git worktree (set KIT_BIN_DIR to install its launcher)`.
  - Closed the existing launcher handle with `with open(...)` to avoid a `ResourceWarning`.
- `tests/test_install_worktree_cmd.py`: 6 unit and subprocess tests covering linked worktree root/subdir, `.git` file, agent worktree paths, main checkout install/update, preserving pre-existing `~/.local/bin/<cmd>` and `board`, and `KIT_BIN_DIR` override.

### Verification
- Post-merge targeted tests: `test_install_worktree_cmd` 6/6 OK, `test_install_update` 2/2 OK, `test_install.py` 0 failed.
- Live worktree dry-run in `/home/anon/board-a1`: logged `SKIPPED command \`board\`: /home/anon/board-a1 is a git worktree (set KIT_BIN_DIR to install its launcher)`.
- Real-project dry-run (K2): `python3 -I /home/anon/board-a1/install.py /home/anon/harmonize --update --dry-run` exited 0 (read-only).

task:
When a part subagent runs `install.py . --update` inside a linked git worktree (e.g. `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/worktrees/...` or `.claude/worktrees/...`), `install_cmd()` in `install.py` only checks `under_tempdir(t)` and overwrites `~/.local/bin/<cmd>` to point at the ephemeral worktree, breaking the one-word launcher once the worktree is removed.

1. In `install.py` (`install_cmd`), detect linked git worktrees (`.git` is a file, or `git rev-parse --git-dir` differs from `--git-common-dir`, or path under `/.gemini/antigravity-cli/worktrees/` or `/.claude/worktrees/`) and skip writing `~/.local/bin/<cmd>` when `KIT_BIN_DIR` is not explicitly set, logging a clear `SKIPPED command ... is a git worktree` line (matching `under_tempdir`).
2. Add unit tests in `tests/test_install_worktree_cmd.py` covering: a linked git worktree skips `~/.local/bin/<cmd>` and leaves an existing launcher untouched; a main checkout still installs/updates it; explicit `KIT_BIN_DIR` still overrides the skip.
title: install_cmd skips linked git worktrees so ~/.local/bin/<cmd> is never overwritten by a part
verdict: Installing or updating from a linked git worktree now skips writing the default user launcher unless an explicit launcher folder is set, keeping the main checkout launcher intact.
